artists.biography:
KillerStar is a rock band founded by Rob Fleming (vocals, guitar, synths) and James Sedge (drums) to channel their shared passion for '70s art-rock, modern alternative textures, and classic rock influences. Emerging as a passion project, the band quickly expanded by attracting an elite lineup of David Bowie's longtime collaborators, including Mike Garson on piano, Earl Slick and Mark Plati on guitar, Gail Ann Dorsey and Tim Lefebvre on bass, Emm Gryner on backing vocals, and Donny McCaslin on saxophone. This ensemble, spanning Bowie's eras from Aladdin Sane to Blackstar, crafts a sound blending crunchy riffs, ethereal harmonies, layered synths, driving grooves, and infectious hooks—forward-looking rather than nostalgic, despite the band's name nodding to Bowie's 2003 track "New Killer Star."

The band's self-titled debut album arrived on March 1, 2024, following the lead single "Should’ve Known Better," which showcased their epic blend of timeless '70s rock with contemporary edges and earned praise from MOJO, The Times, and RnR. Recorded across iconic studios in London, New York, and Los Angeles like RAK and Strongroom, it fueled sold-out shows at London's 100 Club—where they first made their mark—and tours in the UK and USA. Building momentum, KillerStar announced their second album, The Afterglow, set for release on March 20, 2026, via High Wire Records, with Bowie alumni eager to return for more original material recorded in storied spaces.

KillerStar's significance lies in bridging rock's golden eras with fresh innovation, reuniting Bowie's trusted players post-2016 to create new music that stands independently while honoring lineage—marked by high-energy live performances and a growing audience drawn to their sophisticated, guitar-driven art-rock revival.

perplexity.description:
The Afterglow is KillerStar's highly anticipated second album, released on March 20, 2026, following their critically acclaimed self-titled debut. Founded by Rob Fleming and James Sedge to channel their shared love of '70s art-rock and modern alternative sounds, the band has crafted an album that seamlessly blends glam rock, art rock, hook-laden pop, and even touches of jazz. The record features eight brand new songs that incorporate elements spanning four decades of musical evolution—from '70s glam-rock and '80s pop-rock to '90s synth-pop and '00s ambient—all unified by refined melodies, delicate piano passages, heavy guitar riffs, and tribal drumming that marry together in perfect harmony.

The album showcases the exceptional musicianship of KillerStar's renowned collaborators, including several David Bowie alumni: Mike Garson on piano, Earl Slick on guitar, and Mark Plati on bass, alongside additional contributions from Gerry Leonard on guitar, Carey Frank on Hammond organ, and The Webb Sisters on backing vocals. From the opening title track to the closing ballad "Invincible," The Afterglow takes listeners on a breathtaking sonic journey that evokes the spirit of Bowie while establishing its own unique identity. The album received strong support from major UK publications including The Times, Mojo, and RnR, with critics hailing it as a "vibrant and rocking affair" that's "spectacularly produced and professionally delivered."

The record confirms that KillerStar's debut success was no one-off, demonstrating the band as one of the most inspired and imaginative musical projects in contemporary British rock. With standout tracks like "So Easy," "The Rubicon," "There Has To Be A Reason," and "You Do Me No Favours," the album balances high-tempo rock moments and glam-inflected grooves with expansive, atmospheric pieces, all anchored by killer hooks and lyrical themes exploring life, love, and remembrance.
